messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas (as of 2024)** | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits apply unless otherwise indicated.
• Rural interstate: 75 mph; urban interstate: 70 mph.
• School zones: 25 mph (or 35 mph if posted). | | **Seat‑belt & Child Restraint** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (BAC ≥ 0.02 %). | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the driver on the right has priority.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks. | | **Headlights** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather. | | **Toll Roads** | • Electronic toll collection (TxTag) required on most toll roads. | | **Parking** | • No parking within 20 ft of a fire hydrant.
• Parking in a handicap space requires a valid permit. | | **Lane Discipline** | • Keep to the right lane unless passing.
• Do not drive in the left lane on highways unless overtaking. | | **School Bus** | • Stop when a school bus stops with its red lights flashing and stop sign extended. | | **Traffic Signals** | • Red means stop; green means go; yellow means prepare to stop. | | **Vehicle Registration & Insurance** | • Must display registration sticker and proof of insurance. | | **Roadside Assistance** | • Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) provides roadside assistance for registered vehicles. | **Where to Find Official Texts** - Texas Transportation Code (Title 7, Chapter 5) – full statutory text. - Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) website – regulations, forms, and updates. - TxDOT – road rules, signage standards, and enforcement guidelines. **Common Enforcement Practices** - Speed cameras on major highways. - Random breathalyzer checks at DUI checkpoints. - Automated license plate readers (ALPR) for traffic violations. Feel free to ask if you need details on a specific law or how to file a complaint!
